title: Commodities Brief — 06 Oct 2026
intro:
Commodities trade mixed with industrial metals outperforming on demand optimism while crude oil extends weekly losses despite elevated Brent levels above $100. Safe-haven gold consolidates near record highs as markets await central bank signals and geopolitical developments in the Middle East.
🥇 PRECIOUS METALS
Gold $4170.20 +0.32% | Bias: LONG | Key levels: $4150 support / $4200 resistance. Price action remains constructive near all-time highs with shallow intraday pullback reversing. Silver $61.30 +0.71% showing relative strength with positive settlement momentum, outpacing gold on industrial demand tailwinds. Platinum $1722.30 +0.90% extends gains for second session, benefiting from supply constraints and automotive sector optimism.

sections.heading: ⚡ ENERGY
sections.content:
WTI $88.65 -0.87% | Bias: NEUTRAL-BEARISH | Key levels: $87 support / $91 resistance. Crude continues weekly decline despite production concerns, weighed by demand uncertainty. Brent $100.14 -0.18% holding triple-digit pricing but losing momentum from recent highs. Brent-WTI spread at $11.49 remains historically elevated, reflecting persistent Mideast risk premium and logistics differentials. Natural Gas $3.08 +0.46% rebounds modestly after strong weekly gain of 3.81% on storage dynamics.
🌾 AGRICULTURE
Wheat $696.75 +0.65% building on 2.05% weekly advance as supply concerns persist from Black Sea region and adverse weather impacts key growing areas. Corn $499.75 +0.50% steadies after weekly dip, finding support near $500 psychological level. Soybeans $1284.00 +0.25% flat on settlement, consolidating in tight range ahead of harvest pressure.

sections.heading: 🎯 TRADE IDEAS
sections.content:
LONG: Silver entry $61.00 | SL $59.50 | TP $64.50 — outperforming precious complex with industrial demand support and positive technicals above breakout level.
LONG: Copper entry $6.65 | SL $6.45 | TP $6.95 — momentum strength on infrastructure spending expectations and China stimulus measures driving base metals rally.
SHORT: WTI Crude entry $89.00 | SL $91.50 | TP $85.00 — bearish weekly structure intact, demand concerns outweighing supply risks, resistance overhead.

sections.heading: ⚠️ RISKS
sections.content: Escalating Middle East conflict could spike energy prices and disrupt regional supply chains, invalidating bearish oil positioning. Unexpected hawkish central bank pivot would pressure industrial commodities and strengthen dollar headwinds across the complex.
